title: Business Central Under the Hood episode 6: We Have Too Many Events!

chapters.title: Code Customization Era and Its Challenges
Introduction of Events and Migration to Cloud
Event Growth History and Current Scale
Problems with Event Density and Code Maintenance
Event Overload and Events as Code Customization
Extensibility Mechanisms and Moving Toward Interfaces
Introduction to Componentization and System Application
Modular Architecture and Business Foundation Layer
Code Organization, Namespaces, and Breaking Changes Strategy
Technical Debt Removal, Schema Cleanup, and Future Componentization

features.name: Integration Events
features.description: Events introduced as an alternative to code customization, allowing developers to subscribe to events placed in specific locations without modifying source code, eliminating the merge problem from code customization.

features.name: Workflow Events
features.description: The first usage of events was for the workflow feature, with approximately 300 highly curated events placed in commonly extended areas like sales posting and journal posting.
caveats: Only 300 initial events, which was a small fraction of what would eventually be needed

features.name: GitHub-driven Event Requests
features.description: A community-driven approach where partners request needed events through GitHub issues, with over 90% of current events being partner-requested rather than Microsoft-initiated.
caveats: Over 90% of events are partner-requested, indicating Microsoft's reactive rather than proactive approach

features.name: Event Scale in Current Version
features.description: Version 25 contains approximately 22,500 events total, showing linear growth since version 15 after initial exponential growth from the initial 300 events.
caveats: Growth continues but has slowed

features.name: Event Usage Telemetry
features.description: Cloud telemetry analysis shows 3,400 unused events, 5,600 single-environment events, and 53% (11,000) of events used in fewer than 100 environments, indicating significant over-provisioning.
caveats: Data based only on cloud usage, not on-premise

features.name: Event Distribution Analysis
features.description: Of 7,500 total objects, 15% contain no code, events are concentrated in about one-third of remaining objects, and 50% of objects that could contain events do not have any.
caveats: Events are highly concentrated in specific objects

features.name: High Event Density in Core Objects
features.description: Some objects like sales posting codeunit contain over 600 events, creating maintenance challenges where almost every line of code change risks breaking compatibility due to event dependency.
caveats: Creates minefield for bug fixes and refactoring
Events are density of one event per five lines of code in some places

features.name: Event Cleanup Initiative
features.description: Proposal to remove unused events, particularly the 3,400 unused events in cloud environments, with clear partner communication about removal plans.
features.status_evidence_quote: we could choose to remove those um so we can tell Partners R we are going to remove some events you know it's coming
caveats: This is a future consideration, not yet implemented

features.name: Extensibility objects
features.description: Basic extensibility mechanisms including page extension, table extension, and report extension that allow adding extra fields to existing objects.

features.name: Extensible enums
features.description: Extensible enumerations that can be extended through interfaces, providing a better extensibility mechanism than events in many cases.

features.name: Interfaces for extensibility
features.description: Interface-based extensibility where partners can provide their own implementation if allowed, considered a more controlled and powerful way of extending than events.
caveats: Provides a clearer contract than events
More controlled way of extending than events

features.name: Handled events
features.description: A type of event that allows partners to skip Microsoft code and provide their own implementation, functioning similarly to code customization.
caveats: Not considered a friendly way of extending
Acts as code customization which was supposed to be avoided

features.name: Refactoring toward interfaces
features.description: Strategy to move away from event-based extensibility toward interface-based design in newer features and refactored legacy code, resulting in 10 times fewer events.
caveats: Only applies to newer features and componentized areas
Legacy code still contains many events

features.name: System Application
features.description: A technical foundation layer containing utility functionalities like HTTP requests, Azure Key Vault, and file I/O that is non-business-domain, platform-like, and now built as over a hundred individual modules packaged as one app.
caveats: Built as 100+ modules internally but shipped as single app for convenience
Physically open source and on GitHub

features.name: Business Foundation layer
features.description: A new foundational layer introduced in version 24 containing cross-domain ERP features like number series and audit codes that are used across all business domains but not specific to any one domain.
caveats: Work is ongoing to refactor features like Dimensions into Business Foundation
Pulling Dimensions into Business Foundation would involve extracting setup and core dimension logic

features.name: Module Refactoring and Code Rewriting
features.description: When building modules, the team rewrites most of the code rather than copying features. This includes fixing issues from original designs and improving features. Public APIs are split into separate objects and documented.
caveats: Significant work is required to refactor features
Documentation must be maintained for all public APIs

features.name: Source Code Organization with Namespaces
features.description: The code is organized into separate folders and namespaces to improve discoverability and navigation. Namespaces help new and experienced developers understand where features belong and what dependencies exist.
caveats: Implementation is ongoing
Reduces but does not eliminate code complexity

features.name: Obsolescence Scheme with Deprecation Period
features.description: When introducing breaking changes, the team marks code as obsolete and provides partners 12 to 18 months to uptake before removing the old code. Partners receive warnings during recompilation.
caveats: Many changes end up being breaking despite efforts to avoid them
Strict guidelines exist around major breaking changes

features.name: Pre-Processor Symbols for Obsolescence
features.description: Compiler tool used to manage obsolete code by wrapping old code with pre-processor symbols. Allows compilation in two ways: with old code (current shipped version) and with symbols enabled (new code) to remove technical debt at the moment of obsolescence.
caveats: Requires automated process to remove old code from source
Ongoing effort to maintain zero debt principle

features.name: Automated code removal at compilation
features.description: Both old and new code versions are supported during compilation using preprocessor symbols, then an automated process removes the old code at the moment of obsolescence rather than pushing debt forward.

features.name: Clean schema preprocessor symbol
features.description: A new preprocessor symbol called clean schema is introduced to mark obsoleted database fields, enabling automated cleanup of the SQL schema alongside the removal of old code references.
caveats: Retroactive application required for fields obsoleted before this feature was introduced

features.name: Scheduled SQL schema cleanup every fifth release
features.description: Every fifth release, obsoleted fields will be cleaned up from the SQL schema to prevent code clutter, with a minimum retention period before deletion to allow partners time to adapt.
caveats: Fields are retained for at least 2.5 years before removal

features.name: Componentization architecture
features.description: The goal is to break Business Central into smaller modular applications, each with a single purpose and documented API, allowing partners to focus on specific module interfaces rather than understanding 6,000 objects.
caveats: Not yet fully realized
Replaceable components are a future goal

features.name: Replaceable component modules
features.description: A long-term vision where partners could provide their own version of a given component and swap it in, such as a custom HR module or other business functions.
caveats: Not yet implemented
Finance module replacement noted as unlikely

features.name: Selective module installation
features.description: Future capability to install only needed modules at a specific customer installation, avoiding unnecessary module loading, reducing footprint, memory usage, and removing unused UI elements and code paths.
features.status_evidence_quote: there's a future where we could um not install all these modules uh more lean apps so like if you specific installation at a
caveats: Uncertain performance impact
No guarantee of performance improvement
